newsitem.title: UK: UK will reverse any EU work week ruling - Heseltine.
newsitem.headline: UK will reverse any EU work week ruling - Heseltine.

text.p: Britain is determined to reverse any ruling of the European Court forcing it to accept a maximum 48 hour week for employees, deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Monday.

The Court is expected to rule on Tuesday that the European Union's working time regulation applies to Britain despite its opt-out from the EU's Social Chapter because it is a health and safety measure.

Heseltine told BBC Radio he did not believe British economic recovery would be imperilled if the court ruled as expected, partly because "in the short term there are ways in which you can modify the immediate effect".
But Heseltine said in the longer term Britain was determined to get the ruling reversed at the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) which is currently revising the way in which the EU operates.
"We will take this matter up at the IGC and we intend to make sure that it disapplies to this country," he said.

Asked whether this meant Britain would disrupt the IGC to get its way, he added: "It is not a question of disruption. We are in Europe for Britain's self interest and when we get to the IGC we will fight for Britain's corner." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
